newsitem.title: USA: Chino copper workers plan further Phelps protest.
newsitem.headline: Chino copper workers plan further Phelps protest.

text.p: Workers at Phelps Dodge Corp's Chino copper mine will hold a further protest Thursday as their union, the United Steelworkers, file further charges against the company.

"There is a great deal of animosity there," USW lead negotiator Robert Guadiana said. "Attendance policy is going to hell in a handbasket, safety is suffering and things are not very pleasant at Chino."
Phelps' Treasurer Tom Foster said:"The mine is operating fine and safety is fine also."

USW said Friday that AFL-CIO unions and affiliated organizations meet Wednesday in Phoenix to declare their support for copper workers at Chino, followed by a demonstration outside Phelps' head office in the city on Thursday afternoon.

Last week USW filed three charges against Phelps with the National Labor Relations Board in Phoenix, which dealt with the termination of an employee for union activities, the suspension of another for 15 days, and "unlawful surveillance" by company guards, Guadiana said.
Foster said he had not seen the charges but knew of the episodes they related to.
"Before we do anything like terminating employees, we give it a very thorough investigation," Foster said. "We are very careful not to break the law."
The outcome of an earlier charge, probably due later this week, will determine how the union proceeds with stalled labor talks at Chino, Guadiana said.
That complaint alleged that Phelps failed to provide information about pay in non-unionized copper plants.
Chino's 500 employees have been working without contract since June 30 last year. Phelps insists its pay freeze offer is final. The mine produces some 160,000 short tons of copper a year.
"We just wish the union would let our employees vote on the contract," Foster reiterated.
